summary: Learn the building blocks of Azure AI Gateway, create a gateway with a Microsoft Foundry model in the portal, the Azure CLI, or Bicep with azd, and make your first model call, all in about five minutes.

text: Azure AI Gateway gives your apps and agents one governed endpoint for models and tools. In five minutes you create a gateway, put a Microsoft Foundry model behind it, and call that model the way an app does: with the gateway's URL, an alias in the model field, and a runtime API key. Click through the AI Gateway portal, paste a few Azure CLI commands into Azure Cloud Shell, or clone a Bicep template and deploy it with one azd up . Set up once, in the portal, in Cloud Shell, or with azd up. Then every call goes through the gateway: it checks the key, routes the alias, and signs in to Foundry with its own identity. # Before you begin You need an Azure subscription where you can create resources and role assignments, for example Owner , or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator . The gateway gets a role on your Foundry account, so that it can call the model with its own identity. Each track lists the tools that it needs at its start. The Azure CLI and Bicep + azd tracks take a location: eastus2 , or another region from Find the available regions . They also create the Foundry account in that region, so pick one where gpt-6-luna is available too. Each track includes every setup step that it needs, so you can paste it into Cloud Shell as it is. The Setup guide explains these steps, and the later labs link to it. # How it works Every call that goes through AI Gateway uses the same building blocks. In this quick start you create one of each. title: How Azure AI Gateway works
summary: A 20-minute visual tour of the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management. Follow one request through the gateway, meet models, aliases, MCP servers, policies, and identities, and pick the learning path that fits your role.
text: Every team that ships generative AI hits the same questions. Which models may we call, and with which keys? Who spent the tokens? How do we stop one agent from starving everyone else, or from calling a tool it should never touch? The AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management answers them in one place: apps and agents call one gateway, and the gateway decides who gets in, which model or tool answers, what each call may cost, and what gets recorded. Narrated walkthrough: how Azure AI Gateway works (3 min) Apps, agents, and coding agents call one gateway. The gateway authenticates them, applies policies, routes model calls through aliases, federates tools, and emits OpenTelemetry. Note The AI Gateway tier runs in a growing list of regions: run the command in Find the available regions to list them. For the gateway's pricing, see the AI Gateway documentation ↗ . Connected services, such as Microsoft Foundry inference and Application Insights, are billed normally. # Before you begin This lab is a guided reading. You don't need to deploy anything. If you already have a gateway, open the AI Gateway portal ↗ in another tab and follow the portal tour at the end. If you don't have one yet, read on. You create your first gateway in Provision your first AI gateway . # How it works The gateway sits on the path of every model call and every tool call. It has two faces: Data plane : the runtime endpoints your code calls, at https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com . Control plane : the product portal at ai.gateway.azure.com ↗ and the Azure Resource Manager API for the Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways resource type, which you call with the az aigateway Azure CLI extension, Bicep, or any REST client. Building block What it is Example Gateway An AI Gateway resource ( Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways ) in your subscription https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com Backend model A model at a provider, such as a Foundry deployment or an Anthropic model gpt-6-luna at Microsoft Foundry Alias The stable, gateway-wide name clients send in the model field chat MCP server One governed MCP endpoint that federates tools from one or more sources /default/toolservers/<server-name>/mcp Policy A rule on the gateway or on one asset: limits, budgets, safety, filters Token rate limit, Cost limit Access How callers authenticate: API keys or Microsoft Entra ID roles api-key header or Entra token Managed identity How the gateway authenticates to backends Foundry User role on the Foundry account Monitoring OpenTelemetry metrics, logs, and traces for every call Application Insights or any OTLP endpoint Model calls use protocols developers already know. The OpenAI-compatible base URL is https://<gateway-host>/default/models/openai/v1 (append /responses or /chat/completions ), and Anthropic Messages lives at /default/models/anthropic/v1/messages . The gateway passes requests through without translating between OpenAI and Anthropic formats, so call each model on an interface it advertises. # Follow one request Press Play to send a request through the gateway. Then switch scenarios to see where each policy stops a request and which status code the caller gets back. Every applicable policy is evaluated before the gateway forwards a request. If one blocks it, the backend is never called. Three rules explain almost every response you'll see in these labs: Policies run before the backend. If any applicable policy blocks a request, the gateway answers right away and never calls the backend. Each block has a predictable status. 401 for missing or invalid credentials, 403 for IP filters and cost limits ( LlmCostQuotaExceeded ), 429 with Retry-After for token and request rate limits, and 400 for content safety. Everything is recorded. Allowed and blocked calls both show up in Monitoring , along with the policies that affected them. # Models and aliases A backend model is what a provider serves. An alias is what your clients call. Microsoft Foundry imports create an alias for each model by default, and you can add more. Because clients only know the alias, you can move it to a newer or cheaper model without a code change, and the alias keeps its own policies. Two aliases can share one backend model with different policies. Retargeting an alias needs no client change. You can put models from Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints behind aliases. You try it in Route models from several providers behind aliases . # MCP servers and tools Agents need tools as much as models. An MCP server on the gateway gives agents one endpoint and one credential for tools from remote MCP servers, OpenAPI specifications, built-in connectors, and Foundry Toolbox. Tool names are namespaced per source, and tool availability decides which tools clients can see and call. One MCP endpoint federates tools from several sources. Tool availability and policies apply to every call. # Policies and scopes You add a policy at gateway scope , where it applies to every compatible asset including assets you add later, or to individual assets : a backend model, an alias, or an MCP server. Pick an asset below to see every policy that applies to it. Policy Applies to When it blocks Token rate limit Models and aliases 429 with Retry-After Request rate limit Models, aliases, and MCP servers 429 with Retry-After Cost limit Models and aliases 403 LlmCostQuotaExceeded Content safety Models, aliases, and MCP servers 400 IP filter Models, aliases, and MCP servers 403 Agent 365 tool threat protection MCP servers Denies the tool call At gateway scope, the policy type decides which assets are relevant. A gateway-scope cost limit, for example, tracks one budget across all models. # Identities on both sides The gateway separates who is calling from how the gateway reaches the backend . text: Your platform team is about to put every model and tool that the company's apps and agents use behind one governed entry point. Before anyone can publish a model, issue a key, or set a budget, you need the gateway itself. In this lab you create a shared AI Gateway, find its runtime URL and managed identity, and learn your way around the portal so you're ready for the rest of the labs. Narrated walkthrough: create an AI Gateway in the portal and tour it (3 min) One gateway per environment is the usual starting point. Every later lab publishes models, tools, keys, and policies on it. # Before you begin Tip On the Bicep + azd track, azd up creates the resource group and the gateway and names them for you, so you can skip the variables at the end of this section. Do these one-time tasks from the Setup guide first. Every later lab reuses them. Check your subscription and permissions : for example Contributor on the resource group, or on the subscription if you create a new resource group. For the portal track: a browser and your Azure account. For the CLI and Bicep + azd tracks and the Verify steps: choose where to run commands , sign in , install the aigateway extension , and register the resource providers . Find the available regions , and pick one where the Foundry models of the later labs are available too. Recommended reading: How AI Gateway works . # Set your variables Set these variables once. Every track and the Verify section reuse them. Bash PowerShell Copy Important Create the resource group in the same region as the gateway, so that defaults line up. The gateway name must be 1–24 characters: letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen. # How it works An AI Gateway is an Azure Resource Manager resource of type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways . You manage it in the AI Gateway portal ↗ , which is separate from the Azure portal, or through Azure Resource Manager with the CLI, REST, or Bicep. Each gateway has a companion connector gateway ( Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways ) with the same name. There's no capacity to size, so the only real decisions are the name, the region, and the resource group. Property Value Resource type Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways (API version 2025-09-01-preview ), plus Microsoft.Web/connectorGateways with the same name Regions The list grows over time. List them as in Find the available regions Name 1–24 characters: letters, digits, and hyphens. It becomes the first label of the runtime host name Runtime URL https:// + properties.frontend.defaultHostname , for example https://<gateway>.eastus2-01.ai.gateway.azure.com Runtime routes Models under /default/models/… , MCP servers under /default/toolservers/<server>/mcp Outbound identity A system-assigned managed identity, used to call Foundry and other Microsoft Entra–protected backends SKU Consumption , which az aigateway create and the Bicep templates set. A template that omits sku creates a Premium gateway Provisioning time A few minutes, often less Everything you publish later lives in the gateway's default workspace. The gateway applies access, policies, and telemetry before it routes to models and MCP servers. # Create the gateway Pick one track. Each track produces the same result: a gateway named <gateway> in <resource-group> , with a system-assigned managed identity. Then choose the subscription, a Resource group ( New or Existing ), and the Region . Under Advanced , keep Enable system-assigned managed identity selected, Public network access set to Enabled , and Public routing . text: The first product team wants to use gpt-6-luna , which already runs in your Microsoft Foundry account. You don't want to hand every team the Foundry endpoint and a provider key. In this lab you publish the deployment through your gateway, give the team a runtime API key of its own, and make the first call from the playground, a shell, and code. The gateway authenticates to Foundry with its own managed identity, so the app never sees a Foundry credential. The gateway checks the caller's key, applies policies, calls the backend with its own identity, and records telemetry on the way back. # Before you begin Tip On the Bicep + azd track, azd up creates its own gateway, Foundry account, model, and key, so you can skip this section. text: Your team wants to try gpt-6.1-sol , but every app already sends "model": "chat" , and nobody wants a big-bang switch. In this lab you put the current model and the new one behind the same alias, send a fifth of the traffic to the new model, count where the requests land, and then use priority to choose which model is preferred. The apps never change the model name they send. Priority picks the tier. Weight splits the traffic inside it. # Before you begin Tip On the Bicep + azd track, azd up creates its own gateway, both models, the alias, and a key, so you can skip this section. You need only Cloud Shell or the azd tools . Complete Publish a Foundry model and make your first call . You need the gateway, a runtime API key, and the gpt-6-luna backend model. Lab 02 also gave the gateway the Foundry User role on your Foundry account, which covers the new deployment in this lab. Permission to change the gateway, for example Contributor on its resource group, and to create deployments in the Foundry account. The Azure CLI with the aigateway extension , signed in , and jq for the Bash snippets. The PowerShell commands need PowerShell 7 or later. Optional: Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases explains aliases in more depth. For the scripts and samples: the labs repo, cloned . Run them from the lab folder, ~/ai-gateway/labs/22-model-routing . Set these variables once. Every track and the Verify section reuse them. Bash PowerShell Copy The CLI and Bicep tracks of lab 02 name the provider foundry-models . A portal import names it after your Foundry account. To check, list the backend models. The Provider column shows the provider of each one. Bash PowerShell Copy Deploy the candidate model in the same Foundry account as gpt-6-luna . Pick a region where the model is available. Model inference is billed per use. Bash PowerShell Copy # How it works An alias holds a list of backend models. text: Chat apps and agents stream their replies: the model sends text a few tokens at a time, so people start reading after a second or two instead of waiting for the whole answer. Streaming used to be a blind spot for governance, because a streamed Chat Completions response only reports token usage when the client asks for it. In this lab you stream through the gateway with curl, PowerShell, and the OpenAI SDKs, read every event the client receives, and then prove that a token limit still counts every streamed token. Token and cost limits are checked before the stream starts. While the stream flows back, the gateway records its token usage for limits, budgets, and Monitoring. # Before you begin Tip On the Bicep + azd track, azd up creates its own gateway, model, key, and the token-limited streaming alias, so you can skip this section. If you skip the token limit steps, you can set those three by hand and skip the Azure CLI. # How it works Add "stream": true to a Chat Completions request and the gateway answers with Content-Type: text/event-stream . The body is a series of server-sent events (SSE): each one is a data: line with a JSON chunk, followed by a blank line. The gateway passes each chunk on as the model produces it, and the response carries x-accel-buffering: no , which tells proxies such as NGINX not to hold it back. This is what a streamed reply from a Foundry model looks like through the gateway: Chunk choices What it carries Prompt filter results Empty [] Content safety results for the prompt. id and model are empty strings. Role One choice delta.role is assistant and delta.content is an empty string. Content deltas One choice delta.content holds the next few characters of the reply. usage is null . Finish One choice finish_reason is stop , or length when the reply hits max_completion_tokens . Usage Empty [] usage with prompt_tokens , completion_tokens , and total_tokens . Sent when the client sets stream_options.include_usage . data: [DONE] Not JSON The end of the stream. Stop reading. Two chunks have an empty choices array, so code that reads choices[0] on every chunk crashes on the first one. Where the gateway counts tokens. A token limit or cost limit is checked before the gateway forwards the request. When a counter is exhausted, the client gets an ordinary JSON error, such as 429 with Retry-After , and no stream starts. Once a stream starts, it runs to the end, even if it takes the counter past the limit; the next request is throttled. While the stream flows, the gateway records its token usage for token limits, cost limits, and Monitoring. Usage without include_usage . Since the September 24, 2026 release ↗ , the gateway makes sure it has a usage record for every streamed Chat Completions response, even when the client doesn't set stream_options.include_usage , so the counters stay accurate. The release notes ask clients that parse the events themselves to accept a usage-only chunk before [DONE] , even when they didn't ask for one. In our test run in October 2026, a client that didn't set include_usage received no usage chunk, yet the token limit counted its tokens exactly as it did for a client that asked. So write your client to work either way: skip chunks with an empty choices array, and take usage from whichever chunk carries it. text: Your gateway now serves several apps from one model deployment. One batch job sends long prompts in a tight loop and eats the deployment's tokens-per-minute (TPM) capacity, so every other app starts to fail. In this lab you give each caller its own token allowance at the gateway, so a noisy neighbor gets a 429 with Retry-After and everyone else keeps working. Each caller identity gets its own token counter. When a counter is exhausted, the gateway answers 429 without calling the backend. # Before you begin Tip On the Bicep + azd track, azd up creates its own gateway, model, and key, so you can skip this section. You need only Cloud Shell or the azd tools . Complete Publish a Foundry model and make your first call . You need a gateway, an imported model, a callable alias, and a runtime API key from Access › Keys . For the CLI and REST tracks: the Azure CLI with the aigateway extension , signed in , and jq for the Bash snippets. Permission to change the gateway, for example Contributor on the resource group. The value in the request model field must match an alias exactly. # How it works A token limit is a policy that the gateway evaluates before it forwards a request. While the counter is under the limit, the request goes through and the tokens in the response are added to the counter. They want every app to have a daily budget in dollars , a bigger envelope for the production support bot, and a separate allowance for a data science lead who signs in with Microsoft Entra ID. In this lab you set that up as a cost limit at the gateway, so a caller who runs out of budget is stopped before the model is called. A cost limit attached to a model budgets spend on that model. Attached at gateway scope, it tracks one budget per caller across all models. # Before you begin Tip On the Bicep + azd track, azd up creates its own gateway, model, and keys, so you can skip this section. You need only Cloud Shell or the azd tools . Complete Throttle tokens per caller with token limits . This lab reuses the Policies › Add policy wizard and the idea of per-caller counters. A cost limit adds that estimate to the caller's counter for the current renewal period. Before it forwards the next request, the gateway checks the counter. Once spend reaches the budget, the gateway answers 403 ( LlmCostQuotaExceeded in the product docs) with the message LLM cost quota is exceeded and never calls the backend. Responses also carry headers with the cost of the call and the remaining budget. Editing the amount keeps accumulated spend. Renewal periods are fixed calendar windows , not rolling windows: a Daily budget starts fresh at the beginning of each day, not 24 hours after the first call. For the gateway's pricing, see the AI Gateway documentation ↗ . Connected services, such as Foundry inference and Application Insights, are billed normally. To You need, for example Create a gateway in the portal or with the Azure CLI Contributor on the resource group, or on the subscription if you create a new resource group. Creating a gateway needs write access to both API Management and connector gateways. Change a gateway that already exists Contributor on its resource group Give the gateway a role on a Foundry account, as most Bicep + azd tracks do Owner , or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator , on the subscription. The templates create a resource group and role assignments, so that the gateway can call your models with its own identity. Each lab lists any other role that it needs under Before you begin . In the portal, a subscription where you can't create gateways shows as disabled in the subscription picker. # Choose where to run commands Azure Cloud Shell ↗ is the quickest way. Open it in Bash or PowerShell: it's already signed in, and it has the Azure CLI, the Azure Developer CLI ( azd ), Git, jq , curl , Python, Node.js, and .NET. Add the aigateway extension , and you're ready for every track. To work on your own machine, install the tools for the tracks you plan to follow: Tool Used by Azure CLI ↗ 2.75 or later The Azure CLI tracks, the Verify steps, and azd env new in the Bicep + azd tracks The aigateway extension The az aigateway commands Azure Developer CLI ( azd ) ↗ The Bicep + azd tracks. Every command comes in a Bash and a PowerShell variant, unless it's the same in both shells. The PowerShell commands need PowerShell 7 or later, as Cloud Shell has; Windows PowerShell 5.1 doesn't run them. # Sign in to Azure Cloud Shell is already signed in, so skip this step there. On your own machine, sign in to the Azure CLI, select the subscription for the labs, and sign in to azd for the Bicep + azd tracks: Bash or PowerShell Copy If your account belongs to more than one tenant, sign in to the tenant that has the subscription instead: Bash or PowerShell Copy Checkpoint az account show --query name -o tsv prints the name of the subscription you selected. # Install the aigateway extension The labs manage gateways with the aigateway extension of the Azure CLI. Install or upgrade it, then check that the CLI loads it. The installer downloads the published release, verifies it, and needs no Azure sign-in. Bash PowerShell Copy Checkpoint The installer printed 🧩 aigateway extension … is installed , and az aigateway version prints the extension version and the API version it calls, 2025-09-01-preview . For those, the labs call the Azure Resource Manager REST API with az rest and say why. # Register the resource providers The gateway lives in the Microsoft.ApiManagement resource provider and its companion connector gateway in Microsoft.Web . Registering a provider needs a role such as Contributor on the subscription. title: Troubleshooting
summary: The errors you might hit in the Azure AI Gateway labs, with their likely causes and fixes: setup and deployment, and every lab.
text: The errors you might hit in the labs, with their likely causes and fixes. Errors from setting up and deploying, such as a missing extension or an unavailable region, are under Setup and deployment , and the others are under their lab. Look for the error code or the message, for example 429 or ValidationError .

sections.title: Setup and deployment
sections.text: Setup guide: The one-time tasks that every lab builds on Symptom Likely cause Fix 'aigateway' is misspelled or not recognized by the system The aigateway extension isn't installed Install the extension , then run az aigateway version . MissingSubscriptionRegistration , or The subscription is not registered to use namespace A resource provider isn't registered in the subscription Register the resource providers , or ask your subscription administrator. LocationNotAvailableForResourceType The location isn't a region where AI Gateway is available Pick a region from Find the available regions . RequestDisallowedByAzure : The selected region is currently not accepting new customers The region has AI Gateway, but your subscription can't create new resources there Pick another region from the list. InvalidResourceGroupLocation from azd up The resource group rg-<environment name> already exists in another region Run azd env new with a new environment name, or delete the old resource group. Your subscription is disabled in the portal's subscription picker You lack write permission for API Management or connector gateways in that subscription Ask for Contributor on the subscription or resource group, or pick another subscription.

sections.title: Quick start
sections.text: Quick start: Your first model call in 5 minutes Symptom Likely cause Fix A subscription is disabled in Create AI gateway You can't write API Management or connector gateway resources in it Pick another subscription, or ask for Contributor on it. AuthorizationFailed on Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments You can create resources but not role assignments Ask for Owner , or Role Based Access Control Administrator , on the resource group. LocationNotAvailableForResourceType AI Gateway isn't available in the region Pick a region from Find the available regions . RequestDisallowedByAzure : The selected region is currently not accepting new customers The region has AI Gateway, but your subscription can't create new resources there Pick another region from the list. InvalidResourceProperties : The specified SKU 'GlobalStandard' for model 'gpt-6-luna 2026-09-22' is not supported in this region gpt-6-luna isn't available in the region Pick a region where the model check in Find the available regions prints GlobalStandard . InsufficientQuota on the model deployment The subscription has no gpt-6-luna capacity left in the region Start again in another region: set LOCATION in the Azure CLI track, or run azd env new with a new name and another --location in the Bicep + azd track. Or free capacity in Foundry ↗ . InvalidResourceGroupLocation from azd up The resource group rg-<environment name> already exists in another region Run azd env new with a new environment name, or delete the old resource group. 403 or 404 from the gateway in the first minute The gateway's role on the Foundry account, or the new alias, is still taking effect Wait a minute and call again. 403 from the backend that doesn't go away The gateway's managed identity has no role on the Foundry account Assign it Foundry User on the account, as in the Azure CLI track's Deploy the model in Foundry step, and wait a few minutes. 401 The key is missing, wrong, or in the wrong header Send it in the api-key header, or as Authorization: Bearer <key> . In the portal, copy it again from Access › Keys . 400 that mentions authentication The request has both an api-key and an Authorization header Send only one of them. The subscription is not registered to use namespace A resource provider isn't registered yet Run the az provider register loop from Start creating the gateway , then try again. GatewayTimeout : The gateway did not receive a response from 'Microsoft.Web' when you create the connector gateway Azure Resource Manager stopped waiting for the connector gateway, which is usually created anyway Run az rest --method get with the same --url , and add --query properties.provisioningState . If it prints Succeeded , continue with the next command.

sections.title: Lab 00: How AI Gateway works
sections.text: Lab 00: How Azure AI Gateway works Symptom Likely cause Fix A model call says the model can't be found The model field doesn't match an alias Copy the alias from Models , or from the code sample in Catalog An Anthropic call fails on the OpenAI endpoint The gateway doesn't translate between protocols Call /default/models/anthropic/v1/messages with anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 You can't create a gateway in your region AI Gateway isn't available there yet Pick a region from Find the available regions Monitoring is empty No telemetry destination Connect Application Insights in Monitoring › Settings

sections.title: Lab 01: Provision a gateway
sections.text: Lab 01: Provision your AI Gateway Symptom Likely cause Fix Your subscription is disabled in the portal's subscription picker You lack write permission for API Management or connector gateways in that subscription Ask for Contributor on the subscription or resource group, or pick another subscription. LocationNotAvailableForResourceType $LOCATION or the template's location isn't a region where AI Gateway is available Pick a region from Find the available regions . The template defaults to eastus2 . RequestDisallowedByAzure : The selected region is currently not accepting new customers The region has AI Gateway, but your subscription can't create new resources there Pick another region from the list. The name is rejected Gateway names are globally unique and limited to 24 characters: letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter Pick another name that follows the rules. AIGatewaySubscriptionGatewayLimitExceeded : …has reached the maximum of 5 AI Gateway resources allowed in this region. The subscription already has five gateways in $LOCATION Delete a gateway you no longer need, or create this one in another available region. InvalidSkuName : Supported AI Gateway SKU names are 'Premium' and 'Consumption'. Your template sets another sku.name , such as AIGateway from older samples Set sku: { name: 'Consumption' } , as infra/gateway.bicep ↗ does. MissingSubscriptionRegistration A resource provider isn't registered in the subscription Register the resource providers , or ask your subscription administrator. Could not resolve host when you call the URL Provisioning or DNS isn't finished Run az aigateway wait -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --created and retry. 'aigateway' is misspelled or not recognized by the system The aigateway extension isn't installed Install the aigateway extension , then run az aigateway version .

sections.title: Lab 02: First model call
sections.text: Lab 02: Publish a Foundry model and make your first call Symptom Likely cause Fix 401 from the gateway The key is missing, misspelled, or deleted Send an active runtime key in the api-key header or as the SDK API key. Create a new key if you lost the value. 400 with Specify either an API key or an Authorization header, not both The client sends an api-key header and an Authorization header, such as an SDK placeholder key Pass the runtime key as the SDK API key and remove the api-key default header. 403 mentioning permissions on the Foundry account The gateway's identity lacks Foundry User , or the assignment hasn't propagated yet Wait a few minutes. If it persists, assign the role as shown in the portal track. 404 with model_not_found model doesn't match an alias exactly Copy the alias from the model's Aliases tab or from Catalog . 400 unsupported_parameter for max_tokens or temperature gpt-6-luna is a reasoning model Send max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens . Set temperature only together with reasoning_effort: "none" . 200 with empty content and finish_reason length Reasoning used the whole max_completion_tokens budget Raise the budget, or send reasoning_effort: "none" for short, direct replies. The Responses API call fails while Chat Completions works The model doesn't advertise the Responses interface Check the supported interfaces on the model details page and call only those. The import wizard doesn't list your account It's already imported into this gateway, or you can't read it in that subscription Check Models for an existing provider, or ask for read access to the account. AuthorizationFailed on roleAssignments during deployment You can't create role assignments on the Foundry account Ask for Role Based Access Control Administrator on the account, or have an owner grant the role.

sections.title: Lab 03: Multi-provider aliases
sections.text: Lab 03: Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases Symptom Likely cause Fix The wizard discovers no models, or times out The base endpoint URL includes /v1 , the header name is wrong, or the provider doesn't serve /v1/models Use https://api.anthropic.com and x-api-key . If the provider can't list models, add them with Individual model . 401 from the gateway The api-key header is missing or holds the Anthropic key instead of a gateway runtime key Send a runtime key from Access › Keys in the api-key header. An authentication error from Anthropic in the response body The stored provider key is wrong or expired, or Include Bearer is selected for Anthropic Update the provider's API key and clear Authentication scheme . 400 that mentions anthropic-version The request doesn't send the anthropic-version header Add anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 . 404 or a "model not found" error The model value doesn't exactly match an alias, or you called the OpenAI route for an Anthropic model Copy the alias from Models , and call /default/models/anthropic/v1/messages . "Callable aliases must be unique" Another alias in the gateway already uses that name Pick a different alias, or retarget the existing one.

sections.title: Lab 04: Federate MCP tools
sections.text: Lab 04: Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint Symptom Likely cause Fix 401 from the MCP endpoint The key is missing, revoked, or sent in the wrong header Send a runtime key from Access › Keys in the api-key header. 404 from the MCP endpoint Wrong server name in the URL, or the server is still provisioning List the servers with az aigateway mcp list -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -o table and use the exact name in /default/toolservers/<server-name>/mcp . 406 or an error about the Accept header The client doesn't accept both JSON and SSE Send Accept: application/json, text/event-stream , or use an MCP SDK. tools/list returns an empty tools array The registration is reachable but no backend returned tools Check each backend's URL with az aigateway mcp source list -g "$RG" --gateway-name "$GATEWAY" -n <server-name> -o table , and check its authentication. The whole server fails when one backend is down That backend is Required Turn Required off for backends that are nice-to-have, or fix the backend. Backends or policies disappeared after a Bicep deployment A Bicep deployment sends a PUT , which replaces an existing registration with the same name Change existing servers with az aigateway mcp update or az aigateway mcp source add and remove , as in the CLI track, or deploy to a new name. mcp create fails with "This MCP registration already exists; use mcp update." A server with that name already exists Change it with az aigateway mcp update or the mcp source commands, or choose another name. mcp source remove fails with "Cannot remove the last source." An MCP server needs at least one backend Keep at least one backend, or delete the server with az aigateway mcp delete . 400 with Unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version The client sent an MCP-Protocol-Version header that isn't in Supported MCP versions Add the version to the list if every backend supports it, or let the client negotiate a listed version. 404 with "Federation tools/list failed: required endpoint '…' returned error: Backend selected protocol version '…' instead of '…'" Supported MCP versions includes a version that this backend doesn't support, and the client negotiated it Keep only versions that every backend supports. In the portal, edit and save each backend to recheck it. 400 with JSON-RPC error -32603 , "The request cannot be completed using the requested protocol version." A 2026-07-28 request reached a backend that doesn't support 2026-07-28 Remove 2026-07-28 from Supported MCP versions until every backend supports it. 400 with JSON-RPC error -32602 , "Required MCP request metadata is missing or malformed." A 2026-07-28 request lacks the Mcp-Method or Mcp-Name header, or params._meta Use an MCP SDK that implements 2026-07-28 instead of hand-written requests. The portal shows "Backend isn't compatible with all configured MCP versions." The backend doesn't report support for every selected version Return to Basic info and change Supported MCP versions , or update the backend. Creating a server fails with 502 Bad Gateway , or a Bicep deployment keeps running Another MCP server in the gateway already uses the same display name Choose a unique display name, for example with the Bicep displayName parameter.

sections.title: Lab 05: Tool allow and block lists
sections.text: Lab 05: Control which tools agents can call Symptom Likely cause Fix A tool you blocked still appears in tools/list Expected. Blocked tools remain visible, but the gateway blocks their execution Call the tool to confirm that it's blocked. To hide a tool, leave it out of the allow list instead. tools/list returns no tools The allow list matches nothing Check the patterns against the exact tool names. initialize returns AccessBlockedByGateway The server access is Blocked Set MCP server access to Active , or run azd env set MCP_SERVER_ACCESS active and azd provision . An allowed tool is blocked A blocked pattern also matches it. Blocked patterns take precedence Make the blocked pattern narrower, for example *code_sample* instead of *sample* . 429 on the first request of a run The previous step used up the window, or a Gateway scope rate limit also applies Wait for Retry-After , and review Policies for every limit that covers the MCP server. Never 429 The policy is on another asset, it was saved moments ago, or the burst spans two windows Check the policy's scope, wait a minute after you save it, and run a longer burst, for example ./infra/trigger-request-rate.sh learn 12 . Other policies vanished after mcp update --policies replaces the whole policies array Always read the current array, merge, then update, as shown in the Azure CLI track. Tool rules or policies set in the portal vanished after azd provision A Bicep deployment sends a PUT , which replaces the whole MCP server Change the azd environment values and run azd provision instead of editing the server in the portal.

sections.title: Lab 06: Token limits
sections.text: Lab 06: Throttle tokens per caller with token limits Symptom Likely cause Fix Every request returns 200 , never 429 The limit is on a different model or alias than the one you call, or the window reset between requests Check that the request model matches an alias of the limited model. Run the burst without pauses. 429 on the very first request Another token limit with a lower allowance applies, for example a Gateway scope policy, or the counter is shared because Counter dimensions is empty Review Policies for every limit that covers the model. Pick Caller identity for per-caller counters. 403 with LlmCostQuotaExceeded A Cost limit blocked the call, not the token limit See Enforce cost budgets . 429 without a gateway token limit The backend deployment ran out of TPM Raise the deployment's capacity in Foundry, or lower per-caller gateway limits so their sum fits. Other policies vanished after the REST call PATCH replaces the whole policies array Always GET , merge, then PATCH , as shown in the REST track. ValidationError with target counterKey counterKey is a string such as "Identity" , uses another value, or is missing Send an array with identity , ipAddress , or both, for example "counterKey": ["identity"] .

sections.title: Lab 07: Cost budgets
sections.text: Lab 07: Enforce cost budgets with per-caller overrides Symptom Likely cause Fix Every request returns 200 , never 403 The cost limit is on a different model than the alias you call, your key has an override, or the model is so cheap that the calls haven't reached the budget Check Applies to on the policy details page, use a key without an override, and lower the budget to 0.001 or send more requests. 403 with LLM cost quota is exceeded on the first request The key already spent more than the new amount in this period (spend is kept when you edit), or a Gateway scope cost limit is exhausted Review every Cost limit in Policies . Raise the amount, or wait for the next renewal period. An Entra override doesn't apply An earlier override matched first, the caller used an API key, or you entered a service principal's application ID Remove the earlier override and add them again in the order you want. Call with an Entra token. Use the service principal's object ID . Caller IP address can't be selected in Counter dimensions The policy has overrides Remove all overrides, or keep Caller identity . 429 instead of 403 A Token rate limit or Request rate limit blocked the call, or the backend ran out of capacity See Throttle tokens per caller with token limits . Other policies vanished after the REST call PATCH replaces the whole policies array Always GET , merge, then PATCH , as shown in the REST track. ValidationError with target counterKey counterKey is a string such as "Identity" , or it's missing Send an array, for example "counterKey": ["identity"] . A cost limit always needs counterKey .

sections.title: Lab 08: Content safety
sections.text: Lab 08: Screen prompts and responses with content safety Symptom Likely cause Fix Ordinary prompts return 400 A threshold is too strict for your traffic, or another content safety policy, such as a Gateway scope policy, also applies Review Policies for every content safety policy that covers the model. Move categories from Strict to Balanced and retest with representative prompts. Nothing is ever blocked The policy is on a different model or alias than the one you call, or a category is Off Check the policy's scope and that the request model matches an alias of that model. 400 that mentions content_filter , or finish_reason is content_filter The Foundry deployment's Content filter acted, not the gateway Review the deployment's content filter in Foundry. The gateway policy is managed separately. 400 that isn't about content The request itself is invalid, for example an unknown model alias Read the error message, and check the request body and the alias. ValidationError such as contentSafety.violenceSeverity must be one of: Low, Medium, High, None. A severity uses a portal label such as Strict or Balanced Use the API values from the table in How it works : Low , Medium , High , or None . Other policies vanished after the PATCH PATCH replaces the whole policies array Always GET , merge, then PATCH , as shown in the CLI and REST tracks.

sections.title: Lab 09: Gateway-wide baselines
sections.text: Lab 09: Set gateway-wide policy baselines Symptom Likely cause Fix Every call returns 403 Your public IP address changed (new network, VPN, or hotspot), or your network reaches the gateway from a different address than the one api.ipify.org reported Check curl -s https://api.ipify.org again and update the IP filter. If you use a proxy or split-tunnel VPN, ask your network team for the egress ranges. Management calls still work, so you can always fix the list. Teammates, pipelines, or hosted agents get 403 Their egress addresses aren't on the allow list Add their CIDR ranges, or remove the IP filter until you know them. Ordinary prompts return 400 Content safety blocked them, from the baseline or from a stricter asset policy Review every Content safety policy that covers the asset in Policies , and retest with representative prompts. 429 much earlier than the baseline allows A tighter token or request rate limit on the model, alias, or MCP server applies Review Policies for every limit that covers the asset. The lowest applicable limit wins. The PATCH returns a validation error about counterKey or scope counterKey is a string such as "Identity" instead of an array, or the shape differs from what the API version expects Use "counterKey": ["identity"] . If it still fails, create that policy once in the portal at Gateway scope, read the shape with the GET , and use it in your script or policy file. Set ALLOWED_CIDRS ... or Use CIDR notation ... from the script ALLOWED_CIDRS is empty, or an entry has no prefix length Set it to comma-separated CIDR ranges, for example "$MY_IP/32" . Other Gateway scope policies vanished after the REST call PATCH replaces the whole policies array Always GET , merge, then PATCH , as shown in the REST track and the script. jq: command not found jq isn't installed Install jq , or use the PowerShell commands.

sections.title: Lab 10: Runtime API keys
sections.text: Lab 10: Issue and rotate runtime API keys Symptom Likely cause Fix A new key gets 401 The value has a space or line break, or an MCP client sends it in Authorization instead of api-key Copy the value again and send it as api-key: <value> . 400 with Specify either an API key or an Authorization header, not both The client sends an api-key header and an Authorization header Send one of them. With an OpenAI SDK, pass the key as the SDK's API key and remove the extra header. 401 right after Rotate key in the portal Portal rotation replaces the primary value immediately Give the client the value from API key rotated successfully . Next time, use the CLI secondary-value flow. "The key was created, but its value couldn't be retrieved." You don't have Microsoft.ApiManagement/aigateways/apiKeys/listSecrets/action Use Rotate key to get a new value, or ask someone with that permission, such as a Contributor, to read it. check-key prints not checked with HTTP 404 The gateway doesn't know the alias in AI_GATEWAY_MODEL , so it never checked the key Set AI_GATEWAY_MODEL to an alias from Models , for example the one from lab 02. A key that worked gets 401 , and nobody rotated it The key is suspended Check state with the list command, and set it back to active if the suspension is over. check-key prints key accepted, but the call failed The key works, but AI_GATEWAY_MODEL isn't an alias you can call, or a policy blocked the request Set AI_GATEWAY_MODEL to an alias from Models , for example the one from lab 02. Forbidden from az keyvault secret set or secret show You have no data-plane role on the vault, or the role assignment hasn't applied yet Assign Key Vault Secrets Officer on the vault and wait a few minutes. Monitoring shows no caller identities Monitoring isn't configured, or the time range has no traffic Complete Monitor usage, cost, and traces , send requests with each key, and widen the time range.

sections.title: Lab 11: Entra ID and RBAC
sections.text: Lab 11: Go keyless with Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC Symptom Likely cause Fix 401 on every Entra call The token is expired, or it was issued for another audience, such as Azure Resource Manager Request a new token for https://azure-api.net/aigateway ( .default for app-only callers). Check aud in the decoded token. 403 right after you assigned the role Role assignments take several minutes to apply Wait and retry with a fresh token. In the playground, use Back to playground after reviewing access. 403 for one model or MCP server only The role is scoped to a different alias or MCP server, or the role doesn't cover it (Models User on an MCP server, Tools User on a model) Assign a compatible role at the gateway or at that alias or MCP server. 403 even though the role is correct A gateway policy (for example a cost limit), the request proxy, or the backend rejected the call Read the error code in the response body before changing permissions. LlmCostQuotaExceeded comes from a cost limit. AuthorizationFailed when you create the assignment You have Contributor , which can't write role assignments Ask an Owner , User Access Administrator , or Role Based Access Control Administrator to assign the role. DefaultAzureCredential failed to retrieve a token No sign-in is available to the credential chain Run az login , or sign in to the Azure extension in your IDE, then rerun the sample.

sections.title: Lab 12: Backend identities
sections.text: Lab 12: Call backends with managed identities Symptom Likely cause Fix 403 mentioning permissions on the Foundry account right after the switch The role assignment hasn't propagated, or it's at a different scope than the Foundry account Wait a few minutes. Check az role assignment list --assignee "$IDENTITY_PRINCIPAL_ID" --scope "$FOUNDRY_ID" -o table . Calls fail after the switch and the role is in place clientId holds the principal (object) ID, or the identity isn't attached to the gateway Use the identity's Client ID , and check that az aigateway identity show -g "$RG" -n "$GATEWAY" --query userAssignedIdentities lists the identity. az aigateway identity assign fails with an authorization error You can't assign that identity to resources Ask for Managed Identity Operator on the identity. az aigateway identity show reports that no identity is assigned to the gateway The gateway has no managed identity Enable it with az aigateway identity assign in Check the system-assigned identity , then grant it Foundry User . Calls fail after you detach an identity or disable the system identity An asset still uses that identity Check View access › Backend access before you remove an identity, and switch those assets first. AuthorizationFailed on roleAssignments You can't create role assignments on the Foundry account Ask for Role Based Access Control Administrator on the account, or have an owner grant the role.

sections.title: Lab 13: Monitoring
sections.text: Lab 13: Monitor usage, cost, and traces Symptom Likely cause Fix "Enable all telemetry signals" on the dashboard Metrics, logs, or traces is turned off Select Open Monitoring settings and set all three endpoints, or disable monitoring and configure it again with Application Insights. "This legacy exporter no longer activates OTLP signals" in Settings The exporter has kind applicationInsights , for example from the sample's Bicep or a setup before 2026-08-28 Select Settings › General › Disable monitoring , then Configure telemetry again with the same Application Insights resource. Assign Monitoring Metrics Publisher role fails You can't create role assignments on the destination Ask an Owner to grant the role on the Data Collection Rule, or to run the setup. Discover OTLP endpoints fails with "Could not resolve the Data Collection Rule" OTLP support was just enabled and Azure is still provisioning it Wait a few minutes, then select Retry . "Model token and estimated cost data are incomplete until you add a Prometheus access token" The portal can't read the metrics workspace with your session Paste a token from az account get-access-token --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv into Prometheus access token . Dashboard and queries are empty No traffic in the selected range, or ingestion is still catching up Widen the time range, wait a few minutes, and run the traffic script again.

sections.title: Lab 14: OpenTelemetry chargeback
sections.text: Lab 14: Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry Symptom Likely cause Fix No Token claim attributes section in Settings The exporter is the legacy applicationInsights kind Disable monitoring and configure it again, as in Monitor usage, cost, and traces . The entra rows return 401 or 403 Wrong token audience, or no AI Gateway Models User role yet Get the token for https://azure-api.net/aigateway , check the role assignment, wait a few minutes, and get a new token. Entra callers show as Unattributed on Models tid or oid isn't exported to Metrics Select Metrics for both and send new traffic. Earlier requests stay unattributed. The chargeback query returns no rows Telemetry hasn't arrived, the Logs signal is off, or your API reports usage under other names Wait a few minutes, then run OTelLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | take 5 and compare the Attributes with the query. Tenant or ClientApp is empty for Entra rows The claim wasn't exported to Logs when the request ran Enable Logs for the claim and send new traffic. The Prometheus query returns 401 or 403 Your account can't read the Azure Monitor workspace Ask for a data read role on the Azure Monitor workspace, such as Monitoring Data Reader , then get a new token.

sections.title: Lab 15: Agent frameworks
sections.text: Lab 15: Connect agent frameworks to models and tools Symptom Likely cause Fix 401 from the model or MCP endpoint The key is missing, wrong, or revoked, or the header isn't sent Check AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in .env and that the key exists under Access › Keys . A value set in your shell overrides .env . 404 from the MCP endpoint AI_GATEWAY_MCP_SERVER doesn't match an MCP server name Copy the name from MCP servers , or the endpoint from the server's page. A 4xx error that mentions the model AI_GATEWAY_MODEL isn't a callable alias Copy the alias exactly from the model's Aliases tab. The agent answers without citing any URL The MCP server publishes no tools, or tool controls block them Run list_tools.py from Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint and check the server's tool controls. 429 responses A token limit or rate limit on the alias, MCP server, or gateway Expected when a policy applies. Wait for Retry-After , or raise the limit. ModuleNotFoundError The virtual environment isn't active Activate .venv and run pip install -r requirements.txt again.

sections.title: Lab 16: Foundry hosted agent
sections.text: Lab 16: Deploy a Foundry hosted agent behind AI Gateway Symptom Likely cause Fix 400 "Specify either an API key or an Authorization header, not both" The code sends the key as the SDK's API key and also in an api-key header Pass the key only as the SDK's api_key , and remove the api-key default header from the model client. 401 from the MCP endpoint The key went in Authorization: Bearer The MCP endpoint takes keys only in the api-key header, as in main.py . 401 from the model endpoint The key is wrong, suspended, or deleted Check hosted-agent in Access › Keys , load the value again, run azd env set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY , then azd deploy . 404 from the model endpoint AI_GATEWAY_MODEL doesn't match an alias Copy the alias exactly from the model's Aliases tab, run azd env set AI_GATEWAY_MODEL , then azd deploy . 429 "Token limit is exceeded" A token limit on the alias, such as the one from this lab Wait for the time in the message, or remove the policy. 429 from tool calls A request rate limit on the learn server, for example from Control which tools agents can call Wait for the Retry-After time, or remove the policy from the MCP server. RuntimeError: Set AI_GATEWAY_URL An azd environment value is missing Run azd env set for the missing value, then azd ai agent run or azd deploy . The hosted agent still uses an old value Foundry reads environment variables when the agent version is created Run azd deploy after every azd env set . [CodeError] [tool.poetry] section not found during deployment A pyproject.toml without a lock file was added to src/gateway-agent Keep requirements.txt as the dependency file, or commit a uv.lock next to pyproject.toml . azd ai agent run can't download packages, with a certificate error A proxy on your network inspects TLS traffic Set UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=true ( UV_NATIVE_TLS=true in older uv versions) so uv trusts your system certificates, then run it again.

sections.title: Lab 17: Coding-agent plugin
sections.text: Lab 17: Build on your gateway with coding agents Symptom Likely cause Fix /ai-gateway:discover isn't recognized The plugin isn't installed or the client hasn't reloaded it Repeat the install for your agent, then restart it. Check with copilot plugin list in GitHub Copilot CLI or gemini extensions list in Gemini CLI. The plugin can't list models, or Azure returns 401 or 403 az is signed in to another tenant or subscription, or your account can't read the gateway Run az account show , then az account set --subscription <subscription-id> . Ask for read access to the gateway. The plugin stops at the credential step Your account can't list key secrets on the gateway Create or get a key as in Before you begin , and tell the agent to read it from AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY . 404 Resource not found from the gateway The URL is missing the /default/ segment Use <gateway URL>/default/models/openai/v1 or <gateway URL>/default/toolservers/<name>/mcp . unknown_model The model name isn't one the gateway publishes, the client uses another protocol than the model supports, or a GitHub Copilot SDK older than 1.0.0 drops the key header Use the name that discover reported or your alias. Pin github-copilot-sdk>=1.0.0 . 401 from the gateway The key is missing or deleted, or an MCP call sends it as a bearer token. The MCP endpoint reads keys only from the api-key header. Send the key in the api-key header. Create a new key if you deleted it. 400 "Specify either an API key or an Authorization header, not both" The client sends the key in api-key and also an Authorization header, as SDKs do when you pass a placeholder key Send only one. For the model endpoint, pass the runtime key as the SDK's API key and drop the extra api-key header. KeyError: 'AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY' .env wasn't loaded, often because PowerShell saved it with a byte order mark Export the variable in your shell, or save .env as UTF-8 without a byte order mark. 429 A token limit or the backend's quota The wiring works. See Throttle tokens per caller with token limits . A tool server shows 0 tools The server exposes no tools, or tool availability hides them Check the server's tools in the portal, or see Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint .

sections.title: Lab 18: Private networking
sections.text: Lab 18: Lock down backend traffic with private networking Symptom Likely cause Fix The create dialog flags the subnet, or the create request fails with a subnet error The subnet is in another subscription or region, smaller than /27 , not delegated to Microsoft.App/environments , used by another gateway or resource, or its NSG lacks the 443 rules Fix each item. The NSG needs outbound TCP 443 allow rules to the Storage and AzureKeyVault service tags. The create request fails with AIGatewaySubnetNotDelegated : "Virtual network integration with subnet ID '…' requires the subnet to be delegated to 'Microsoft.App/environments'." The subnet isn't delegated, or it's delegated to another service, such as Microsoft.Web/serverFarms Delegate the subnet to Microsoft.App/environments , then create the gateway again. The portal's subnet check shows a warning: "Subnet delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms" The portal check still expects the old delegation Expected. Keep Microsoft.App/environments and continue. "Virtual network integration for Azure AI Gateway can only be configured during creation." You tried to add, change, or remove private routing on an existing gateway Create a new gateway with private routing. Model calls through the new gateway fail after you turn off Foundry public access The gateway resolves Foundry to its public IP: the zones aren't linked to the integrated virtual network, the private endpoint has no DNS zone group, or the gateway was created without private routing Check the A records and zone links, and confirm that properties.backend.subnet.id points to the integration subnet. The gateway from the earlier labs, or another app, now gets 403 from Foundry It reaches Foundry over the internet, and Foundry's public access is disabled Expected. Use a dedicated Foundry resource for this lab, or re-enable public access when you finish. The first call after the import returns 401 or 403 from the backend The Foundry User role assignment hasn't propagated yet Wait a few minutes, and confirm that the role is assigned to the new gateway's principal ID on the Foundry resource. Public network access › Disabled is greyed out, or a PATCH to Disabled doesn't stick Private frontend access isn't available for AI Gateway yet Expected. Protect the public endpoint with keys or Microsoft Entra ID and an ipFilter policy. Deleting the resource group or the virtual network fails because the subnet is in use The service is still releasing the gateway's integration subnet Wait a few minutes after the gateway is gone, then delete again.

sections.title: Lab 19: Tool threat protection
sections.text: Lab 19: Protect tool calls with Agent 365 threat protection Symptom Likely cause Fix Every protected call returns ToolEvaluationIdentityRequired The call has no bearer token, or the token isn't a delegated user token. App-only tokens and runtime keys can't be used for OBO. Sign in with az login as a user, get a token for https://azure-api.net/aigateway , and send it as Authorization: Bearer . Check that the token has an scp claim. tools/call returns HTTP 401 or 403 with a bearer token The user has no data-plane role on the MCP server, or the assignment hasn't applied yet Assign AI Gateway Tools User at the MCP server or gateway scope and wait a few minutes Calls return ToolEvaluationUnavailable The token exchange or the evaluation failed, timed out, returned an invalid verdict, or the evaluator was unavailable Retry later. If it persists, confirm the Microsoft Defender or Microsoft Purview license and the Defender policy mode with your security team, and share the correlationId . A benign call returns ToolEvaluationDenied Defender or Purview flagged the request or the result Review the call with your security team using the correlationId . If the tool already ran (after-invocation stage), don't retry it automatically. You can't add a second tool threat protection policy to the server Each MCP server can have only one tool threat protection policy Keep the existing policy, or delete it and add a new one with the stages you want Tool calls got noticeably slower Each enabled stage adds an evaluation round trip Keep both stages where you need them, and use only Before tool invocation where results are trusted A script stops with HTTP 503 and {"error":"App port is not ready"} The gateway is still starting after azd up or azd provision Wait 30 seconds and run the script again. A policy you added in the portal vanished after azd provision A Bicep deployment sends a PUT , which replaces the whole MCP server Change the azd environment values and run azd provision instead of editing the server in the portal.

sections.title: Lab 20: Agent 365 governance
sections.text: Lab 20: Govern MCP servers with Agent 365 Symptom Likely cause Fix The gateway's MCP servers don't appear under Agents › Tools Consent isn't granted, or the instance is on an API Management v1 tier Have a tenant administrator turn on Azure API Management service and AI Gateway under Agents › Settings › Gateways . Use a v2 tier or the AI Gateway tier. The server's Tools tab can't list its tools The server doesn't have a static list of allowed tools, for example it uses Allow all tools In the AI Gateway portal, choose Select exact tools on the server's Tools step. Otherwise, block tools in the AI Gateway portal. You can't block individual tools The instance is on an API Management v2 tier Tool-level blocking needs the AI Gateway tier. Block the whole server instead. A blocked tool still runs for some agents Those agents call the MCP server directly, not through the gateway Point every agent at the gateway's MCP endpoint and restrict direct access to the backend An agent keeps retrying a blocked tool The agent ignores isError Check result.isError and the ToolNotAvailable denial code, and stop retrying that tool Calls still fail after you unblock Another control blocks them, such as the gateway's Blocked tools , MCP server access , or a policy Check the server's Basic info and Tools steps and its policies in the AI Gateway portal

sections.title: Lab 21: Enterprise reference
sections.text: Lab 21: Deploy an enterprise reference architecture Symptom Likely cause Fix The deployment fails with InsufficientQuota , or the model or version isn't available The region has no GlobalStandard quota for gpt-6-luna , or doesn't offer that version Lower modelCapacity , request quota, or change modelName , modelVersion , or --location in your parameter file and command. The gateway's provisioningState ends in Failed Azure hit an activation or managed identity conflict, often after a gateway with the same name was deleted moments before Delete the failed gateway and its connector gateway, wait about three minutes for the identity to be cleaned up, and deploy again. The smoke test prints Waiting for the model route until it fails with 401 , 403 , or 404 The new Foundry User role assignment or the model route hasn't propagated yet Wait a few minutes and run the smoke test again. If it still fails, run the backend identity checks in Verify . Settings in Monitoring shows "This legacy exporter no longer activates OTLP signals" You deployed with enableLegacyAppInsightsExporter set to true Select Settings › General › Disable monitoring , then Configure telemetry again with the same Application Insights resource. apply-baselines fails with a validation error from the PATCH A field in baselines.json doesn't match the current API contract, for example counterKey as a string instead of an array such as ["identity"] Create the policy once in the portal at Gateway scope, read the workspace with az rest , and copy that shape into baselines.json . azure/login fails with AADSTS70021: No matching federated identity record found The token subject doesn't match a federated credential Check that the subject is exactly repo:<github-org>/<github-repo>:environment:<name> and that the GitHub environment name matches the job's environment: .

sections.title: Lab 22: Priority and weighted routing
sections.text: Lab 22: Route an alias across models by priority and weight Symptom Likely cause Fix "Select models with at least one common API format." The selected backend models don't share an interface, for example an Anthropic Messages model and an OpenAI Chat Completions model Put models that share an interface in the same alias. "Weight must be a whole number from 1 to 100.", Each target's weight must be a whole number from 1 to 100. , or weight must be between 1 and 100. A weight is 0 , negative, or above 100 To stop traffic to a model, raise its priority number or remove it. "Priority must be a whole number from 0 to 100.", Each target's priority must be a whole number from 0 to 100. , or priority must be between 0 and 100. A priority is outside 0 to 100 Use 0 for the preferred tier and higher numbers for the others. "Each backend model can appear only once." or backendModels must not contain duplicate model identities. The same backend model is listed twice Combine the entries and adjust the weight. This model alias already exists; use model-alias update. You ran az aigateway model-alias create for an alias that exists Run az aigateway model-alias update with the same arguments. All requests go to one model The models have different priorities, so only the lowest number receives traffic Give the models the same priority to split by weight. 404 with DeploymentNotFound The candidate backend model points to a Foundry deployment that doesn't exist Create the deployment, or fix deployment.resourceId on the backend model. 429 from the preferred model The preferred deployment is out of capacity, and the gateway returns the error Retry in the client, add capacity, or spread traffic with weights at the same priority.

sections.title: Lab 23: Streaming responses
sections.text: Lab 23: Stream responses and count every token Symptom Likely cause Fix IndexError: list index out of range in Python, or Cannot read properties of undefined in TypeScript The code reads choices[0] on the prompt filter chunk or the usage chunk, which have no choices Skip chunks whose choices array is empty, as the samples do. The whole reply appears at once curl runs without -N , PowerShell uses Invoke-RestMethod , or a proxy buffers the response Use curl -N , read the stream with HttpClient as stream-chat.ps1 does, and turn off response buffering in your proxy. No usage chunk at the end of the stream The client didn't set stream_options.include_usage Set it when your app needs the numbers. The gateway counts the tokens for its limits either way. 400 with The 'stream_options' parameter is only allowed when 'stream' is enabled. The request sets stream_options without "stream": true Send both, or neither. 429 JSON response instead of a stream A token limit on the alias, the model, or the gateway is exhausted Wait for Retry-After seconds. The limit is checked before the stream starts, so no partial reply is lost. The SDK sample never shows a 429 The OpenAI SDKs retry 429 responses automatically and honor Retry-After That's the behavior you want in an app. To see each 429 , create the client with max_retries=0 (Python) or maxRetries: 0 (TypeScript). Every request in the burst returns 200 The policy isn't active yet, or the burst used another alias Check that STREAM_ALIAS matches the alias with the limit, wait a minute, and run the burst again.

sections.title: Lab 24: GitHub Copilot BYOK
sections.text: Lab 24: Use your gateway's models and tools in GitHub Copilot Symptom Likely cause Fix HTTP 401 or "Authentication failed with provider" The key is wrong, suspended, or deleted, or the new key isn't active yet Check the key's state in Access › Keys , wait a minute after you create it, and paste it again. 400 on every request from a custom client The request sends both Authorization and api-key Send one of them. Copilot sends Authorization: Bearer only. 404 , or a "model not found" error The model name isn't an alias on the gateway, for example the portal import's <foundry-account-name>/gpt-6-astra Publish the gpt-6-astra alias, or set the model ID to the alias that exists. The model doesn't appear in VS Code or the app The gateway has no /models list to discover, or VS Code hasn't reloaded the file Add gpt-6-astra by hand, then run Developer: Reload Window in VS Code. The model is missing from the picker in Agent mode toolCalling is missing or false Set "toolCalling": true on the model. VS Code or the app doesn't offer your own models at all Your Copilot Business or Enterprise organization hasn't allowed custom models Ask an administrator to enable them. Replies are empty or cut off, or tool calls fail The surface uses Chat Completions with a reasoning model Set the API to Responses: apiType in VS Code, COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=responses for the CLI, wireApi in the SDK. 429 Too Many Requests Copilot used the key's 100,000 tokens for this minute Wait for the Retry-After interval, or raise the token limit. The CLI's first interactive prompt doesn't respond A slow first connection Press Ctrl + C and send the prompt again. Two GPT-6 Astra entries in VS Code's model picker Copilot's built-in model and yours share a name Give yours a distinct name , such as GPT-6 Astra (AI Gateway) . The MCP server doesn't start, or returns 401 The key is sent as a bearer token, or ${AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY} is empty where the CLI or the app runs Send the key in the api-key header. Export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in the terminal, or make it available to the app and reopen it. copilot -p doesn't use the Learn tools, or says they were denied One-shot mode can't ask for approval Add --allow-tool='ai-gateway-learn' . A task with the Learn tools hits 429 or uses many tokens Each Learn result is 25 to 50 KB Ask for fewer lookups, publish fewer tools, or raise the token limit. VS Code lists MCP servers that you didn't add VS Code discovers servers configured in other apps Set chat.mcp.discovery.enabled to false .
